"'''Boom Boom Pow'''" is a song recorded by American group [[Black Eyed Peas|the Black Eyed Peas]] for their fifth studio album ''[[The E.N.D.]]'' (2009). It was written by group members [[will.i.am]], [[apl.de.ap]], [[Taboo (rapper)|Taboo]] and [[Fergie (singer)|Fergie]], being produced by will.i.am. The song features a vocal sample from the 1990 song "Reach Out" by British house duo [[Sweet Mercy]] featuring singer [[Rowetta]].<ref name="Rogers">{{cite web|url=https://thegentlewoman.co.uk/library/rowetta|title=Rowetta|last=Rogers|first=Jude|work=[[The Gentlewoman (magazine)|The Gentlewoman]]|access-date=October 24, 2021|archive-date=August 7, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210807194446/https://thegentlewoman.co.uk/library/rowetta|url-status=live}}</ref> It was released as the [[lead single]] from ''The E.N.D.'' on February 22, 2009, by [[Interscope Records]].

"Boom Boom Pow" topped the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] for 12 weeks, making it the group's first number-one single on the chart. It is the second longest-running single to stay atop the chart in 2009, beaten only by their own "[[I Gotta Feeling]]", which held the top spot for 14 consecutive weeks. The song also topped the charts in Australia, Canada and the United Kingdom, as well as reaching the top ten in more than 20 countries. It was ranked atop the ''Billboard'' Hot 100 year-end chart for 2009, at number seven on the decade-end chart for the 2000s,<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.billboard.com/bbcom/charts/chart_display.jsp?g=Singles&f=Greece#/../../charts-decade-end/hot-100-songs?year=2009|title=Charts|magazine=Billboard|access-date=December 14, 2009|archive-date=June 10, 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080610074032/http://www.billboard.com/bbcom/charts/chart_display.jsp?g=Singles&f=Greece#/../../charts-decade-end/hot-100-songs?year=2009|url-status=dead}}</ref> and at number 51 on the all-time chart.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.billboard.com/articles/list/2155531/the-hot-100-all-time-top-songs?list_page=4=|title=Hot 100 55th Anniversary: The All-Time Top 100 Songs|magazine=Billboard}}</ref> The [[Recording Industry Association of America]] certified it diamond.

Critically acclaimed, "Boom Boom Pow" was nominated for [[Best Dance Recording]] and won [[Best Short Form Music Video]] at the [[52nd Annual Grammy Awards]] (2010). ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' ranked the song at number 14 on their list "Best 25 Songs of 2009".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/news/story/31364221/the_25_best_songs_of_2009/5 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091221061737/http://www.rollingstone.com/news/story/31364221/the_25_best_songs_of_2009/5 |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 21, 2009 |title=Search Articles, Artists, Reviews, Videos, Music and Movies |publisher=Rolling Stone |date=September 15, 2010 |access-date=September 19, 2010}}</ref> As of April 2025, the music video has over 511 million views on [[YouTube]].

"Boom Boom Pow" is a song recorded by American group the Black Eyed Peas for their fifth studio album The E.N.D. (2009). It was written by group members will.i.am, apl.de.ap, Taboo and Fergie, being produced by will.i.am. The song features a vocal sample from the 1990 song "Reach Out" by British house duo Sweet Mercy featuring singer Rowetta. It was released as the lead single from The E.N.D. on February 22, 2009, by Interscope Records.

"Boom Boom Pow" topped the Billboard Hot 100 for 12 weeks, making it the group's first number-one single on the chart. It is the second longest-running single to stay atop the chart in 2009, beaten only by their own "I Gotta Feeling", which held the top spot for 14 consecutive weeks. The song also topped the charts in Australia, Canada and the United Kingdom, as well as reaching the top ten in more than 20 countries. It was ranked atop the Billboard Hot 100 year-end chart for 2009, at number seven on the decade-end chart for the 2000s, and at number 51 on the all-time chart. The Recording Industry Association of America certified it diamond.

Critically acclaimed, "Boom Boom Pow" was nominated for Best Dance Recording and won Best Short Form Music Video at the 52nd Annual Grammy Awards (2010). Rolling Stone ranked the song at number 14 on their list "Best 25 Songs of 2009". As of April 2025, the music video has over 511 million views on YouTube.

sections.heading: Music and lyrics
Release
sections.wikitext: "Boom Boom Pow" was released to U.S. mainstream radio on March 13, 2009. It was released officially on iTunes in the U.S. on March 30, 2009. It was scheduled to be released in the UK on May 25, 2009, however due to three alternative versions of the song entering the UK iTunes Top 50 songs, the Black Eyed Peas version was released two weeks early, on Sunday, May 10. One of their full performances took place at the ''[[American Idol (season 8)#Finale|American Idol]]'' Finale of 2009, during which the Top 13 girls sang "[[Glamorous (Fergie song)|Glamorous]]", and then Fergie came out and sang a small part of "[[Big Girls Don't Cry (Fergie song)|Big Girls Don't Cry]]", eventually switching to "Boom Boom Pow". As of June 2009, an unknown number of North American [[radio]] stations have elected to censor the song's reference to [[satellite radio]].<ref name='satwaves'>{{cite news | first=Brandon | last=Matthews | title=The N.A.B. Convinces Congress That Stealing Is A Good Thing | date=June 4, 2009 | url =http://satwaves.com/blog/2009/06/04/the-nab-convinces-congress-that-stealing-is-a-good-thing/ | work =Satwaves | access-date = June 5, 2009 }}</ref> Most UK radio stations have also been found to distort the word satellite radio, and this is the version that appears on the UK CD single.

sections.heading: Remixes
sections.wikitext:
The official remix of the song is titled "Let the Beat Rock - Boys Noize Remix". The track is produced by [[Boys Noize]] with five versions of the song. These remixes credit recording to Pardraic Kerin and mixing to Dylan "3-D" Dresdow. The official remix features [[50 Cent]], and is structured like so: 50 Cent's verse goes first, then will.i.am's first new verse, then Fergie, later the chorus, Fergie's first verse is repeated, then will.i.am's second verse, later the chorus, Fergie's first verse is repeated, apl.de.ap and Taboo's verse from the original were used, then Fergie's second verse, later the chorus, and the song ends with will.i.am saying "pow". The song only lasts 4:30.

A "Megamix" version was also very popular, and is structured like so: will.i.am's verse from the first version goes first, then 50's verse, later the chorus, then Fergie's, then will.i.am's new second verse, later the chorus, Fergie's first verse is repeated, later the chorus, and the song ends. The song only lasts 3:29. The megamix version features [[Gucci Mane]]. A third version features [[Flo Rida]], a fourth version is a mash-up of the 50 Cent Remix and the Gucci Mane Remix, and a fifth version is remixed by Busta Rhymes and Fatman Scoop. A remix by DJ Ammo and A Poet Named Life is played in the ending credits of the 2009 Summer blockbuster film ''[[G.I. Joe: The Rise of Cobra]]''. At the [[American Music Awards of 2009|2009 American Music Awards]], the guitar riff from "[[Smells Like Teen Spirit]]" by [[Nirvana (band)|Nirvana]] was played after the performance of this song. Another remix of this song was made by [[David Guetta]], titled " David Guetta's Electro Hop Remix". On the fourth season of ''[[America's Best Dance Crew]]'', a District 78 remix of the song was used for the sudden death challenge on the first episode, in the dance-off between Beat Ya Feet Kings, Southern Movement, and Fr3sh. Fr3sh was eliminated. In 2009, [[Jeffree Star]] created a remix with more explicit lyrics, that was originally available as a free download.<ref name="Interview">{{cite web|url=http://www.29-95.com/music/story/jeffree-star-takes-no-prisoners |title=JEFFREE STAR TAKES NO PRISONERS |publisher=29-95.com |access-date=July 23, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090926072038/http://www.29-95.com/music/story/jeffree-star-takes-no-prisoners |archive-date=September 26, 2009}}</ref> The original download link no longer works; however, many videos of live performances are available.<ref>{{cite video |people=Jeffree Star|date=June 29, 2009|title=Boom Boom Pow|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XarMLVhfdcQ}}</ref>

sections.heading: Critical reception
sections.wikitext:
Nick Levine from ''[[Digital Spy]]'' gave "Boom Boom Pow" four out of five stars, saying that "it's a fairly ridiculous robopop stomper featuring no real chorus, ''[[808s & Heartbreak]]''-style beats, lashings of [[Auto-Tune]], techno synths that arrive half-way through and this vintage diss from [[Fergie (singer)|Fergie]]: 'I'm so 3008, you're so 2000 and late.' It may well become grating, but frankly who cares? Right now this just sounds cracking."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.digitalspy.com/music/a155019/black-eyed-peas-boom-boom-pow.html |title=Music - Singles Review - The Black Eyed Peas: 'Boom Boom Pow' |publisher=Digital Spy |date=May 25, 2009 |access-date=September 19, 2010}}</ref> ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' gave the song a positive review, stating that the song "shows The Black Eyed Peas in fine form" and that it was "a knockout".<ref>{{cite magazine|last=Williams|first=Chris|url=http://www.billboard.com/bbcom/reviews-singles/boom-boom-pow-1003953591.story|title=Review: Boom Boom Pow|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard.com]]|date=March 28, 2009|access-date=April 7, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090421134212/http://www.billboard.com/bbcom/reviews-singles/boom-boom-pow-1003953591.story|archive-date=April 21, 2009}}</ref>
*''[[Boston Globe]]'': "Dealt with individually, substance-free, grammatically suspect dance-floor jams like current monster hit 'Boom Boom Pow,' the slinky '[[Imma Be]],' or the fuzzy '[[Missing You (Black Eyed Peas song)|Missing You]]' could be booty-shaking guilty pleasures."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://archive.boston.com/ae/music/cd_reviews/articles/2009/06/15/black_eyed_peas_the_end/ |title=The Black Eyed Peas, 'The E.N.D' - The Boston Globe |publisher=Boston.com |date=June 15, 2009 |access-date=September 19, 2010}}</ref>
*Dot Music: "''E.N.D.'' opener 'Boom Boom Boom' has a long way to go before it even tickles the room, mid-tempo beats cushioning a Fergie vocal that an autotune stuck on override can't sort out."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://uk.launch.yahoo.com/090615/33/221bu.html |title=The Black Eyed Peas The E.N.D Album Review, New album reviews and latest album releases on Yahoo! Music |publisher=Uk.launch.yahoo.com |date=June 15, 2009 |access-date=September 19, 2010}}</ref>
*''[[Entertainment Weekly]]'': "Indeed, indefatigable Auto-Tune anthems like The E.N.D's propulsive lead single, 'Boom Boom Pow' (already the band's most successful to date), seem fueled by some mysterious slurry of dance-floor plutonium and diet Red Bull."<ref>{{cite magazine |author=Greenblatt |first=Leah |date=June 3, 2009 |title=The E.N.D |url=http://www.ew.com/ew/article/0,,20282707,00.html |access-date=September 19, 2010 |magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]] |publisher=[[Meredith Corporation]] |archive-date=March 17, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140317004350/http://www.ew.com/ew/article/0,,20282707,00.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>
*[[Vibe (magazine)|''Vibe'' magazine]]: "However, the intergalactic punch of 'Boom Boom Pow'–BEP's first Billboard chart-topper–has stimulated a slew of cosigns from the likes of 50 Cent, Gucci Mane, and Kid Cudi."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.vibe.com/music/revolutions/2009/06/revs_the_black_eyed_peas_the_end/ |title=Music |publisher=VIBE |date=July 26, 2010 |access-date=September 19, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090703123923/http://www.vibe.com/music/revolutions/2009/06/revs_the_black_eyed_peas_the_end/ |archive-date=July 3, 2009}}</ref>
*''[[The Guardian]]'': "As on their recent No 1 single, 'Boom Boom Pow', electronic clicks and buzzes are used lavishly, and the mood is as positive as ever. Just don't expect to love it immediately."<ref>{{cite news |last=Sullivan |first=Caroline |date=June 5, 2009 |title=The Black Eyed Peas, The E.N.D |work=[[The Guardian]] |location=London |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2009/jun/05/blac-eyed-peas-end-album |access-date=April 26, 2010}}</ref>
*''[[Los Angeles Times]]'': "The titles of the Peas' biggest hits tell the story: the giggle-inducing pun of '[[Don't Phunk With My Heart]],' the cheerily crude anatomical gesture of 'My Humps' and now the Imax-ready sound effects burst of the chart-topping 'Boom Boom Pow.'"<ref>{{cite web |date=June 2, 2009 |title=Album review: The Black Eyed Peas' 'The E.N.D' | Pop & Hiss | Los Angeles Times |url=http://latimesblogs.latimes.com/music_blog/2009/06/album-review-black-eyed-peas-the-end.html |access-date=September 19, 2010 |website=[[Los Angeles Times]] |publisher=}}</ref>
*''[[Rolling Stone]]'': "Whereupon the record segues into the Number One hit 'Boom Boom Pow,' and all hell breaks loose. There are Auto-Tune vocal trills, eerie synth chords, screechy disco-diva wailing, 808 thuds, raps about 808 thuds and a dizzying barrage of doggerel: 'I got that . . . digital spit/Next-level visual shit.' It is an assault on the senses, and on good taste. And it's the best thing The Black Eyed Peas have ever recorded."<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Rosen |first=Jody |date=September 14, 2010 |title=Album Reviews |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/albumreviews/the-e-n-d-the-energy-never-dies-20090608 |access-date=January 6, 2011 |magazine=[[Rolling Stone]] |publisher=[[Penske Media Corporation]]}}</ref>
*''[[The Independent]]'': "Contrary to Fergie's claim on 'Boom Boom Pow' that 'I'm so 3008, you so 2000-and-late', their supposedly innovative electro-beat stylings are tired."<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/music/reviews/album-the-black-eyed-peas-the-end-polydor-1702917.html | work=The Independent | location=London | title=Album: The Black Eyed Peas, The E.N.D (Polydor) | first=Andy | last=Gill | date=June 12, 2009 | access-date=April 26, 2010}}</ref>

sections.heading: Chart performance
sections.wikitext:
In Australia, "Boom Boom Pow" was released on March 30, 2009, and debuted on the [[ARIA Charts]] on April 6. It reached number one, staying there for six weeks. It spent 27 weeks in the Top 20. Australia is the first country in which the song was released. As of October 2015, the song has sold 6.9 million downloads in the US<ref name=us_sales>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.billboard.com/pro/ask-billboard-lady-gaga-first-artist-with-two-7-million-selling/ |title=Ask Billboard: Lady Gaga First Artist With Two 7-Million-Selling Downloads |last=Trust |first=Gary |magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] |publisher=[[Prometheus Global Media]] |date=October 2, 2015 |access-date=October 3, 2015}}</ref> and was certified 4× Platinum by the RIAA. This number of singles sold makes the Black Eyed Peas the second artist to have two singles each selling six million copies or more, following [[Lady Gaga]].<ref name="ReferenceA">{{cite web|last=Grein |first=Paul |url=http://new.music.yahoo.com/blogs/chart_watch/74360/week-ending-may-1-2011-songs-even-divas-struggle/ |title=Week Ending May 1, 2011. Songs: Even Divas Struggle | Chart Watch - Yahoo! Music |publisher=New.music.yahoo.com |date=May 4, 2011 |access-date=January 17, 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110723120454/http://new.music.yahoo.com/blogs/chart_watch/74360/week-ending-may-1-2011-songs-even-divas-struggle/ |archive-date=July 23, 2011}}</ref>

The song debuted at number 71 on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] after garnering heavy airplay. The song rocketed from number 39 to number one in its fourth week on the chart. The single sold 465,000 downloads in its first week of digital release, the third-largest number of download sales in a single week overall, and the largest single-week and debut-download totals by a group in the history of digital-download sales tracking, reaching number one on the U.S. ''Billboard'' Hot 100 and [[Pop 100]]. It became the group's first U.S. number one, holding the spot for twelve consecutive weeks.<ref>{{cite web|url={{BillboardURLbyName|artist=the black eyed peas|chart=Hot 100}} |title=Top 100 Music Hits, Top 100 Music Charts, Top 100 Songs & The Hot 100 |publisher=Billboard.com |access-date=September 19, 2010}}</ref> Having been dethroned to number two by the other Black Eyed Peas' song, "[[I Gotta Feeling]]", it is the second longest running number one song of 2009 on the chart, behind "I Gotta Feeling", and the first song to spend at least twelve weeks at number one since [[Mariah Carey]]'s "[[We Belong Together (Mariah Carey song)|We Belong Together]]" in 2005. The chart week of May 30, 2009 "Boom Boom Pow" became only the fifth song to top both ''Billboard'''s [[Mainstream Top 40]] and [[Rhythmic Top 40]] charts in the same week, reaching an estimated audience of 99 million on U.S. radio that week.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.billboard.com/pro/chart-beat-the-black-eyed-peas-jeremih-beyonce/ |title=Chart Beat: The Black Eyed Peas, Jeremih, Beyonce |publisher=Billboard.com |date=September 14, 2009 |access-date=September 19, 2010 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140829045846/http://www.billboard.com/articles/columns/chart-beat/268581/chart-beat-the-black-eyed-peas-jeremih-beyonce |archive-date=August 29, 2014 }}</ref>

It was the fourth song of the decade to spend at least twelve weeks at number one, and only the twelfth song in the chart's history to spend at least twelve weeks at the top. It is the band's first Rhythmic number one, and their second Mainstream Top 40 number one. "Boom Boom Pow" became the first song in digital history to spend its first twelve weeks of release as the most-downloaded song in America, selling at least 200,000 copies a week for eleven straight weeks.<ref>[http://new.music.yahoo.com/blogs/chart_watch/35570/week-ending-may-31-2009-boom-boom-pow-sets-digital-record/ Week Ending May 31, 2009: "Boom Boom Pow" Sets Digital Record] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120922003849/http://music.yahoo.com/blogs/chart-watch/week-ending-may-31-2009-boom-boom-pow-sets-digital-record.html |date=September 22, 2012 }} Chart Watch by Paul Grein, Retrieved: June 3, 2009</ref><ref>[http://new.music.yahoo.com/blogs/chart_watch/35620/week-ending-june-14-2009-america-eats-its-peas/ Week Ending June 14, 2009: America Eats Its Peas] Chart Watch by Paul Grein, Retrieved: June 17, 2009</ref> ''Billboard'' ranked it as the No. 1 song of 2009.<ref>[[Billboard Year-End Hot 100 singles of 2009]]</ref> It has also topped the charts on the [[Canadian Hot 100]] the same week as on the Hot 100 and on the Australian [[Australian Recording Industry Association|ARIA]] Charts. On the New Zealand [[Recording Industry Association of New Zealand|RIANZ]] chart, the song has peaked at number two. Moreover, it has charted within the top 10 in more than ten countries.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://acharts.us/song/42384 |title=The Black Eyed Peas - Boom Boom Pow - Music Charts |publisher=Acharts.us |access-date=September 19, 2010}}</ref>

On May 17, 2009, it entered the [[UK Singles Chart]] at number one based on almost 75,000 downloads alone. It is the band's second number one in the UK (the other being "[[Where Is the Love?]]" which also reached the top of the chart six years prior). It has also reached number three so far in [[Ireland]]. After being knocked off the number one spot in the [[United Kingdom]] on May 24, 2009, by "[[Bonkers (song)|Bonkers]]" by [[Dizzee Rascal]] and [[Armand Van Helden]], the song remained at the number two slot for 2 weeks before returning to number one on June 7, 2009. "Bonkers" had meanwhile swapped places with "Boom Boom Pow" and took the number two slot. This subsequently marks the first time a song has had two separate runs at the summit of the chart since [[Shakira]]'s "[[Hips Don't Lie]]" in July 2006. Their follow up single in the UK "I Gotta Feeling" also peaked at number one and managed the same feat of having two separate runs at number one on the UK Singles Chart. With sales of over 600,000, the single is currently the sixth best selling of 2009 in the UK. "Boom Boom Pow" is also the 13th best selling R&B song of the 21st century in the UK.
sections.text:
In Australia, "Boom Boom Pow" was released on March 30, 2009, and debuted on the ARIA Charts on April 6. It reached number one, staying there for six weeks. It spent 27 weeks in the Top 20. Australia is the first country in which the song was released. As of October 2015, the song has sold 6.9 million downloads in the US and was certified 4× Platinum by the RIAA. This number of singles sold makes the Black Eyed Peas the second artist to have two singles each selling six million copies or more, following Lady Gaga.

The song debuted at number 71 on the Billboard Hot 100 after garnering heavy airplay. The song rocketed from number 39 to number one in its fourth week on the chart. The single sold 465,000 downloads in its first week of digital release, the third-largest number of download sales in a single week overall, and the largest single-week and debut-download totals by a group in the history of digital-download sales tracking, reaching number one on the U.S. Billboard Hot 100 and Pop 100. It became the group's first U.S. number one, holding the spot for twelve consecutive weeks. Having been dethroned to number two by the other Black Eyed Peas' song, "I Gotta Feeling", it is the second longest running number one song of 2009 on the chart, behind "I Gotta Feeling", and the first song to spend at least twelve weeks at number one since Mariah Carey's "We Belong Together" in 2005. The chart week of May 30, 2009 "Boom Boom Pow" became only the fifth song to top both Billboards Mainstream Top 40 and Rhythmic Top 40 charts in the same week, reaching an estimated audience of 99 million on U.S. radio that week.

It was the fourth song of the decade to spend at least twelve weeks at number one, and only the twelfth song in the chart's history to spend at least twelve weeks at the top. It is the band's first Rhythmic number one, and their second Mainstream Top 40 number one. "Boom Boom Pow" became the first song in digital history to spend its first twelve weeks of release as the most-downloaded song in America, selling at least 200,000 copies a week for eleven straight weeks. Billboard ranked it as the No. 1 song of 2009. It has also topped the charts on the Canadian Hot 100 the same week as on the Hot 100 and on the Australian ARIA Charts. On the New Zealand RIANZ chart, the song has peaked at number two. Moreover, it has charted within the top 10 in more than ten countries.

On May 17, 2009, it entered the UK Singles Chart at number one based on almost 75,000 downloads alone. It is the band's second number one in the UK (the other being "Where Is the Love?" which also reached the top of the chart six years prior). It has also reached number three so far in Ireland. After being knocked off the number one spot in the United Kingdom on May 24, 2009, by "Bonkers" by Dizzee Rascal and Armand Van Helden, the song remained at the number two slot for 2 weeks before returning to number one on June 7, 2009. "Bonkers" had meanwhile swapped places with "Boom Boom Pow" and took the number two slot. This subsequently marks the first time a song has had two separate runs at the summit of the chart since Shakira's "Hips Don't Lie" in July 2006. Their follow up single in the UK "I Gotta Feeling" also peaked at number one and managed the same feat of having two separate runs at number one on the UK Singles Chart. With sales of over 600,000, the single is currently the sixth best selling of 2009 in the UK. "Boom Boom Pow" is also the 13th best selling R&B song of the 21st century in the UK.

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext:
[[File:Boom Boom Pow - Screenshot.jpg|thumb|right|200px|will.i.am in the futuristic-themed video for "Boom Boom Pow" <!--CAUTION: DO NOT REPLACE THE CURRENT SCREENSHOT OF THE MUSIC VIDEO WITH THE PREVIOUS ONE SHOWING 4 MEMBERS OF THE PEAS AS IT FAILS WP:NFCC #8 AND IS AT A VERY LOW RESOLUTION!-->]]

[[Fergie (singer)|Fergie]] had stated at an interview on ''[[The Insider (TV series)|The Insider]]'' that the music video would be shooting the week of March 8, 2009.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.theinsider.com/news/1786971_Fergie_Gives_Firsthand_Account_of_Wedding_Day |title=Fergie Gives Firsthand Account of Wedding Day at The Insider |publisher=Theinsider.com |access-date=September 19, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090409164956/http://www.theinsider.com/news/1786971_Fergie_Gives_Firsthand_Account_of_Wedding_Day |archive-date=April 9, 2009}}</ref> The making of the video was released by MTV on April 8.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mtv.com/videos/news/369929/fergie-calls-the-black-eyed-peas-misfits.jhtml#id=1608887 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090411032140/http://www.mtv.com/videos/news/369929/fergie-calls-the-black-eyed-peas-misfits.jhtml#id=1608887 |url-status=dead |archive-date=April 11, 2009 |title=Fergie Calls The Black Eyed Peas 'Misfits' | News Video |publisher=MTV |access-date=September 19, 2010}}</ref> In an interview to MTV, it was said that "... the concept of the video is the Peas' birth into the digital afterlife," Fergie said. "So the transformation is us going into a sort of birth or cocoon and coming out the other end as forms of energy. It's a parallel to the music industry. Now everything is downloaded." [[will.i.am]] stated that the video was inspired by how digital the world has become and hopes the video portrays "what it would be like if we were actually in the computer, if art was fused in it," he said.  "[It's] analog life from a digital perspective. Becoming technology."<ref>{{cite web|title=Boom Boom Pow Backstage + Interview with The Black Eyed Peas |url=http://www.tabmagnetic.com.ar/news/2009-04-09-125 |date=April 9, 2009 |publisher=tabmagnetic.com |access-date=June 18, 2009 }}{{dead link|date=May 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> The music video was directed by [[Mathew Cullen]] and Mark Kudsi. The video premiered on [[Dipdive]] on April 18, 2009, and was released on iTunes on April 24, 2009.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dipmusic.dipdive.com/#/~/videoplayer/0/undefined/28427/~/ |title=[Dipdive] DipMusic Home |access-date=April 19, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090422052221/http://dipmusic.dipdive.com/ |archive-date=April 22, 2009}}</ref> The video is set in the year of 3008, portraying "how it would be like if we actually lived in computers". This concept was based in a line of the song, in which singer Fergie states "I'm so 3008 / You so 2000 and late".

The video starts with [[Taboo (rapper)|Taboo]] flicking through pictures on a [[HP TouchSmart]], he selects the image of a [[mushroom cloud]]. As the singing starts, images of computer icons, random computer code and some [[ASCII art]] of "THE END" are flashing in the background. The Black Eyed Peas are then seen singing their verses of the song. While this is happening, dancers are seen in striped [[zentai]] suits, dancing to the song, and negative images are turned into positive images; for instance, the explosion cloud turns into a tree swing, the grenade into a microphone, a gun into a trumpet and a nuclear waste barrel played as a drum. The video also features the face used on [[The E.N.D|the album cover]] miming along to various lyrics; the face was designed as an amalgam of all four band members' facial features. Much of the imagery in the video is a [[Homage (arts)|homage]] to [[Rebecca Allen (artist)|Rebecca Allen]]'s 1986 video for the [[Kraftwerk]] song "[[Musique Non Stop]]".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rebeccaallen.com/v2/work/work.php?isVideo=1&wNR=20&ord=alph&wLimit=12 |title={ Musique Non Stop } |publisher=Rebeccaallen.com |access-date=September 19, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110723214302/http://www.rebeccaallen.com/v2/work/work.php?isVideo=1&wNR=20&ord=alph&wLimit=12 |archive-date=July 23, 2011}}</ref> The video was meant to go the full song but they cut it to 3:29. The video won a [[Grammy]] at the [[52nd Annual Grammy Awards]] in the category of [[Best Short Form Music Video]]. As of December 2023, the music video of the song scored over 472 million views on YouTube.

thumb|right|200px|will.i.am in the futuristic-themed video for "Boom Boom Pow" 

Fergie had stated at an interview on The Insider that the music video would be shooting the week of March 8, 2009. The making of the video was released by MTV on April 8. In an interview to MTV, it was said that "... the concept of the video is the Peas' birth into the digital afterlife," Fergie said. "So the transformation is us going into a sort of birth or cocoon and coming out the other end as forms of energy. It's a parallel to the music industry. Now everything is downloaded." will.i.am stated that the video was inspired by how digital the world has become and hopes the video portrays "what it would be like if we were actually in the computer, if art was fused in it," he said.  "[It's] analog life from a digital perspective. Becoming technology." The music video was directed by Mathew Cullen and Mark Kudsi. The video premiered on Dipdive on April 18, 2009, and was released on iTunes on April 24, 2009. The video is set in the year of 3008, portraying "how it would be like if we actually lived in computers". This concept was based in a line of the song, in which singer Fergie states "I'm so 3008 / You so 2000 and late".

The video starts with Taboo flicking through pictures on a HP TouchSmart, he selects the image of a mushroom cloud. As the singing starts, images of computer icons, random computer code and some ASCII art of "THE END" are flashing in the background. The Black Eyed Peas are then seen singing their verses of the song. While this is happening, dancers are seen in striped zentai suits, dancing to the song, and negative images are turned into positive images; for instance, the explosion cloud turns into a tree swing, the grenade into a microphone, a gun into a trumpet and a nuclear waste barrel played as a drum. The video also features the face used on the album cover miming along to various lyrics; the face was designed as an amalgam of all four band members' facial features. Much of the imagery in the video is a homage to Rebecca Allen's 1986 video for the Kraftwerk song "Musique Non Stop". The video was meant to go the full song but they cut it to 3:29. The video won a Grammy at the 52nd Annual Grammy Awards in the category of Best Short Form Music Video. As of December 2023, the music video of the song scored over 472 million views on YouTube.

sections.heading: Alleged copyright infringement
sections.wikitext: In January 2010, [[Chicago]] artist Ebony Latrice Batts, better known by her stage name Phoenix Phenom, alleged the song is simply a copy of her track, "Boom Dynamite" (written by Manfred Mohr). The duo allegedly sent a demo tape to [[Interscope Records]]. They lost the lawsuit against the Black Eyed Peas.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bet.com/photo-gallery/vp12sy/music-stars-and-lawsuits/8jbx0q|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240511054016/https://www.bet.com/photo-gallery/vp12sy/music-stars-and-lawsuits/8jbx0q|url-status=dead|archive-date=May 11, 2024|title=Music Stars and Lawsuits|website=Bet.com|access-date=August 6, 2018}}</ref>
